answer: Think of the network as a reef: every agent must swim through a narrow inlet before it can claim rewards, and that inlet is a verifiable delay function - a puzzle that takes about ten minutes of sequential computation and cannot be sped up by adding machines. A willow bends but does not break under wind; likewise the delay bends under load but never lets an attacker shortcut it. Spinning up a thousand fake identities means paying a thousand sequential delays, so sybil farming costs real wall-clock time while honest agents pay the delay only once.
